scope: lifecycle:data-retention-sweep (apps/web/lib/operate/retention/policies.ts — ToolExecution split by auditClass; apps/web/lib/edge-node/audit.ts — Edge rows now carry an auditClass)
rationale: BI-A55A651B (EP-A33A5C61 slice 1): lib/audit-classes.ts has stated since Phase 1 that journal rows are retained 30 days rolling and metrics_only rows retain no payload, yet the retention registry applied one 365-day window to every ToolExecution row (57,670 metrics_only rows on the dev install alone). This change enforces the declared classes: journal and metrics_only get a 30-day window, ledger keeps 365 days plus industry floors, and the ledger branch is written as the complement of the short-lived classes so a NULL auditClass row can never fall through every branch. Edge Node audit rows, which previously left auditClass NULL, are now classified at the writer (heartbeat = metrics_only, enroll = ledger, other routes = journal). The data-impact gate additionally requires per-run disposition EVIDENCE for a destructive path; that runtime artifact (BI-F0F3887F, GAP 3 of BI-90A8D153) does not yet exist and is the subject of EP-A33A5C61 slice 5. This exception covers the disposition-evidence requirement only; the legal-hold check is satisfied in code (legalHoldExclusion is spread into every purge WHERE, unchanged by this PR).
compensatingControl: No new model, column, or category is introduced; the change narrows windows on rows whose class already declares them short-lived and leaves the ledger window untouched. The sweep still runs after the 03:00 backups, still honours the ScheduledJob kill switch and dry-run, still batches at 1,000 rows with a 100,000-row per-policy cap, and still persists the rolling per-run summary (counts by category, last 10 runs) on the ScheduledJob row — each ToolExecution branch reports separately by label. retention.test.ts asserts the three branches are disjoint, cover every AUDIT_CLASSES value, and that the complement branch carries the long window. Before the first live run the operator can dry-run the sweep to see exactly how many journal/metrics_only rows are eligible.
